from_quote: a writer under the signature of Brutus, in the New York paper, which has been re-published by Messrs. Dunlap and Claypoole, has done this in so masterly a manner, that it would be superfluous in me to add anything on this subject
rationale: Centinel (dated November 5, 1787) refers the reader to Brutus for the impracticability of one free government over so extensive a territory and the case for a confederation of republics. Brutus I (October 18, 1787) argues that subject; Brutus II (November 1) treats a bill of rights, so the essay is worked out from date and subject.
